key_insight: PISO combines the known gradient part with a tracked estimate of the unknown residual, so zeroth-order noise is controlled by tracking error rather than by the full missing gradient magnitude.
engineering_relevance: This makes partially observed optimization practical for systems like performative learning, RL, and bilevel problems where only some derivatives are available and function evaluations are expensive.
method: Uses the available gradient component directly and updates a running estimate of the residual.
Centers each zeroth-order probe on the residual estimate to reduce variance and create a contraction step.
Supports Gaussian or spherical probes with just one probe direction, two function samples, and one known-gradient sample per iteration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence rates of O(d^2ε^-6) with Lipschitz gradients and O(d^2ε^-5) with an additional Lipschitz-Hessian assumption, plus empirical gains across five benchmark settings.
watch_item: Performance depends on the residual-tracking quality and on independently sampled function evaluations, so noisy or correlated oracle calls may weaken the method's advantages.
paper_title: Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization via Zeroth-Order Residual Tracking
